checks.summary:
# Candidate-family specification disposition audit

Scope: the eleven feature specifications named by System's four candidate families, including their shared published-skill-first source. This is a bounded retention/removal assessment, not a repository-wide conformance audit. Selected surviving clauses and supersession notices were compared with current owning-model boundaries and direct references/implementation surfaces. One necessary unmigrated obligation is sufficient to reject whole-file deletion; this audit does not approve every historical sentence. Matching test-spec files were not independently audited for deletion.

Result: zero whole-spec removal candidates established; four mixed-source candidates for partial consolidation and seven retained sources. No spec was deleted. Partial retention is a proposed content split, not permission to trim an unreviewed file now. Final clause transfer/removal and dependent checks belong to the receiving Design and Delivery package.

| Specification | Disposition | Concrete surviving meaning / supersession and next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| specs/skill-invocation-commands-for-adapters.md | Retain | R3–5 distinguish included OpenCode skills from curated command aliases; generation/invocation behavior is not defined by Skill's content model. scripts/adapter_distribution.py generates alias metadata and selected alias paths. Design's later authoring-name amendment must be applied without reinstating retired aliases. Distribution/FU-013 receives exact generation and invocation transfer. |
| specs/stop-tracking-generated-public-adapter-skill-bodies.md | Partially retain | R0/R0a/R0b/R1/R2 describe the version-specific transition and historical boundary; these are not fresh rollout prerequisites. R8–17 retain tracked support-surface limits, absent generated bodies, complete generated archives, untracked archives and install navigation. Constitution and current metadata reinforce the source distinction but do not fully replace the distribution contract. Distribution/FU-013 must retain those ongoing rules and dispose completed transition prose explicitly. |
| specs/target-native-init.md | Retain | TNI-R1–8 define positional commands and safe rejection of removed --adapter; TNI-R19/20 and TNI-R72/73 govern state implication and safe rewriting. TNI-DES-01–06 preserve managed authoring replacement and recovery. Current Design explicitly consumes those clauses. Installation/FU-013 must own them before source removal. |
| specs/multi-adapter-init-and-proxy-aware-download.md | Partially retain | Its old --adapter command/default state-write requirements are explicitly superseded by target-native-init's opening Supersession boundary and TNI-R6–8. MAI-R7–21 and later trust/download clauses retain descriptors, roots, bundled metadata verification, archive identities, proxy/local-trust and extraction safety unless specifically amended. Transfer those into Installation/Distribution; do not delete the whole spec based on obsolete command examples. |
| specs/rigorloop-cli-lockfile.md | Partially retain | Codex-only/default-write command assumptions are superseded by later multi-adapter and target-native init amendments. R40–53 retain malformed/unknown-state rejection, drift checks and conflict behavior; tree hashing remains an installation contract. packages/rigorloop/dist/lib/lockfile.js and managed-authoring-replacement.js are the relevant implementation consumers, while CLI's model covers workflow recording and explicitly excludes general installation transfer. Installation/FU-013 must reconcile the surviving state contract before removal. |
| specs/release-process-contract.md | Retain | REL-R1–3 distinguish routine publication from policy change; REL-R14/14a/63 retain release gates and explicit emergency deferral requirements. Release profiles do not replace release authority. Release/FU-013 receives these obligations; no release model currently exists. |
| specs/release-transaction-automation.md | Retain | R1–5 specify profile location, identity, target set, publication/evidence requirements and profile-owned release state. scripts/release_transaction.py loads and validates those operational profiles. Release/FU-013 must transfer transaction semantics, not just rename profile references. |
| specs/test-layering-and-change-scoped-validation.md | Retain | R1/R2 and related selector/wrapper provisions describe concrete selection modes and scoped versus broad execution. scripts/ci.sh still constructs selector commands and interprets phase/preflight results. Later direct-hosted and v2 amendments qualify old behavior; they do not prove all remaining execution contracts retired. FU-012 must inspect remaining modes before choosing exact transfer or retirement. |
| specs/validation-execution-performance-and-preflight.md | Retain | R1–5 require preflight ordering, named blockers, diagnostics and explicit diagnostic override before broader work. Wrapper phase handling remains present. Test's proportionality criteria and Review and Closeout reuse policy do not completely define execution behavior. FU-012 receives the remaining execution decisions; no policy waiver from document cleanup. |
| specs/validation-idempotency-and-cache-hit-safety.md | Retain | R1–12 and R13–30 distinguish eligible commands, prior passes, content/implementation/policy identity, missing inputs and conservative fallback. scripts/validation_cache.py still computes those identities; scripts/test-validation-cache.py exercises a spec-named path in a temporary fixture, including missing/present states. That fixture is not a direct reader of this checkout's spec and cannot by itself justify permanent path retention. Workflow's stored-format retirement and CLI explicitly leave unrelated cache policy separately owned. FU-012 must resolve actual reachability, retained safety and owner before retirement; semantic reuse in RC-SR-15 is not a complete cache implementation contract. |
| specs/published-skill-first-repository-simplification.md | Partially retain | The current Design already selects R14/R17–20/R22 cleanup exceptions and removes duplicate ADR/architecture representation later. R4/R5/R7–10/R21/R25/R28 and exact R26/R27/R29 supersession boundaries retain distribution, release, materialization, CI and proof meaning. Skill/Test/RC/CLI cover parts only. Retain the mixed operational remainder under its actual owners; current initiative completes only its reviewed source-map slice. |

Consumer interpretation: a normative reference, implementation of a requirement, operational read and incidental citation are different facts. Searches found mostly Design references for these filenames; lack of a hard-coded filename in executable code is not absence of a contract. No passing runtime, package or release result is asserted. No publication, cache retirement, test deletion or whole-directory removal is selected.

Next ownership: FU-012 for remaining execution sources; FU-013 for Distribution/Installation/Release transfers; current necessary-design change for its already selected published-skill-first cleanup. The earlier System candidate revision still requires independent Design rereview before Delivery reliance. This audit is author evidence, not renewed approval.
